title: Bartolomeu Dias round the Cape of Good Hope, 1487–88
summary: Two caravels and a supply ship out of Lisbon, down the coast of Africa past Diogo Cão's last padrão, blown out to sea by a storm, and back onto the coast at Mossel Bay; the first Europeans to round the southern tip of Africa.

events.label: Mossel Bay: the first Europeans ashore in southern Africa
events.text: After a month out of sight of land, the ships turned north and found a coast running east: they had rounded the Cape without seeing it. At the watering place they called São Brás, Khoikhoi herders drove the landing party off with stones, and one of them was killed by a crossbow bolt.

events.label: Padrão de São Gregório at Kwaaihoek, the farthest point
events.text: Having been blown round the Cape without seeing it, Dias sailed on east along the coast, until his tired crew begged him to turn. He raised a stone pillar, a padrão, to St Gregory here and went home, seeing the Cape on the way. Its fragments were found at Kwaaihoek in 1938.
